tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

79	## Build tags

81	### Build with json replacement
82

100	go build -tags=sonic .
101	```
102	
103	### Build without `MsgPack` rendering feature
104	
105	Gin enables `MsgPack` rendering feature by default. But you can disable this feature by specifying `nomsgpack` build tag.
106	
107	```sh
108	go build -tags=nomsgpack .
109	```
110	
111	This is useful to reduce the binary size of executable files. See the [detail information](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/pull/1852).

113	## Routing
114	
115	> Learn how to define routes, handle parameters, and organize endpoints.
116	
117	### Using GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS
118	
119	```go
120	func main() {
121	  // Creates a gin router with default middleware:
122	  // logger and recovery (crash-free) middleware
123	  router := gin.Default()
124	
125	  router.GET("/someGet", getting)
126	  router.POST("/somePost", posting)
127	  router.PUT("/somePut", putting)
128	  router.DELETE("/someDelete", deleting)
129	  router.PATCH("/somePatch", patching)
130	  router.HEAD("/someHead", head)
131	  router.OPTIONS("/someOptions", options)
132	
133	  // By default, it serves on :8080 unless a
134	  // PORT environment variable was defined.
135	  router.Run()
136	  // router.Run(":3000") for a hard coded port
137	}
138	```
139	
140	### Parameters in path
141	
142	```go
143	func main() {
144	  router := gin.Default()
145	
146	  // This handler will match /user/john but will not match /user/ or /user
147	  router.GET("/user/:name", func(c *gin.Context) {
148	    name := c.Param("name")
149	    c.String(http.StatusOK, "Hello %s", name)
150	  })
151	
152	  // However, this one will match /user/john/ and also /user/john/send
153	  // If no other routers match /user/john, it will redirect to /user/john/
154	  router.GET("/user/:name/*action", func(c *gin.Context) {
155	    name := c.Param("name")
156	    action := c.Param("action")
157	    message := name + " is " + action
158	    c.String(http.StatusOK, message)
159	  })
160	
161	  // For each matched request Context will hold the route definition
162	  router.POST("/user/:name/*action", func(c *gin.Context) {
163	    b := c.FullPath() == "/user/:name/*action" // true
164	    c.String(http.StatusOK, "%t", b)
165	  })
166	
167	  // This handler will add a new router for /user/groups.
168	  // Exact routes are resolved before param routes, regardless of the order they were defined.
169	  // Routes starting with /user/groups are never interpreted as /user/:name/... routes
170	  router.GET("/user/groups", func(c *gin.Context) {
171	    c.String(http.StatusOK, "The available groups are [...]")
172	  })
173	
174	  router.Run(":8080")
175	}
176	```

179	
180	```go
181	func main() {
182	  router := gin.Default()
183	
184	  // Query string parameters are parsed using the existing underlying request object.
185	  // The request responds to a URL matching: /welcome?firstname=Jane&lastname=Doe
186	  router.GET("/welcome", func(c *gin.Context) {
187	    firstname := c.DefaultQuery("firstname", "Guest")
188	    lastname := c.Query("lastname") // shortcut for c.Request.URL.Query().Get("lastname")

190	    c.String(http.StatusOK, "Hello %s %s", firstname, lastname)
191	  })
192	  router.Run(":8080")
193	}
194	```

274	### Upload files
275	
276	#### Single file
277	
278	References issue [#774](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/774) and detail [example code](https://github.com/gin-gonic/examples/tree/master/upload-file/single).
279	
280	`file.Filename` **SHOULD NOT** be trusted. See [`Content-Disposition` on MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Disposition#Directives) and [#1693](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/1693)
281	
282	> The filename is always optional and must not be used blindly by the application: path information should be stripped, and conversion to the server file system rules should be done.
283	
284	```go
285	func main() {
286	  router := gin.Default()
287	  // Set a lower memory limit for multipart forms (default is 32 MiB)
288	  router.MaxMultipartMemory = 8 << 20  // 8 MiB
289	  router.POST("/upload", func(c *gin.Context) {
290	    // Single file
291	    file, _ := c.FormFile("file")
292	    log.Println(file.Filename)
293	
294	    // Upload the file to specific dst.
295	    c.SaveUploadedFile(file, dst)
296	
297	    c.String(http.StatusOK, fmt.Sprintf("'%s' uploaded!", file.Filename))
298	  })
299	  router.Run(":8080")
300	}
301	```
302	
303	How to `curl`:
304	
305	```bash
306	curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/upload \
307	  -F "file=@/Users/appleboy/test.zip" \
308	  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data"
309	```

311	#### Multiple files
312	
313	See the detailed [example code](https://github.com/gin-gonic/examples/tree/master/upload-file/multiple).
314	
315	```go
316	func main() {
317	  router := gin.Default()
318	  // Set a lower memory limit for multipart forms (default is 32 MiB)
319	  router.MaxMultipartMemory = 8 << 20  // 8 MiB
320	  router.POST("/upload", func(c *gin.Context) {
321	    // Multipart form
322	    form, _ := c.MultipartForm()
323	    files := form.File["upload[]"]
324	
325	    for _, file := range files {
326	      log.Println(file.Filename)
327	
328	      // Upload the file to specific dst.
329	      c.SaveUploadedFile(file, dst)
330	    }
331	    c.String(http.StatusOK, fmt.Sprintf("%d files uploaded!", len(files)))
332	  })
333	  router.Run(":8080")
334	}
335	```
336

338	
339	```bash
340	curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/upload \
341	  -F "upload[]=@/Users/appleboy/test1.zip" \
342	  -F "upload[]=@/Users/appleboy/test2.zip" \
343	  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data"
344	```

346	### Grouping routes
347	
348	```go
349	func main() {
350	  router := gin.Default()
351	
352	  // Simple group: v1
353	  {
354	    v1 := router.Group("/v1")
355	    v1.POST("/login", loginEndpoint)
356	    v1.POST("/submit", submitEndpoint)
357	    v1.POST("/read", readEndpoint)
358	  }
359	
360	  // Simple group: v2
361	  {
362	    v2 := router.Group("/v2")
363	    v2.POST("/login", loginEndpoint)
364	    v2.POST("/submit", submitEndpoint)
365	    v2.POST("/read", readEndpoint)
366	  }

368	  router.Run(":8080")
369	}

372	### Redirects
373	
374	Issuing a HTTP redirect is easy. Both internal and external locations are supported.
375	
376	```go
377	r.GET("/test", func(c *gin.Context) {
378	  c.Redirect(http.StatusMovedPermanently, "http://www.google.com/")
379	})
380	```
381	
382	Issuing a HTTP redirect from POST. Refer to issue: [#444](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/444)
383	
384	```go
385	r.POST("/test", func(c *gin.Context) {
386	  c.Redirect(http.StatusFound, "/foo")
387	})
388	```
389	
390	Issuing a Router redirect, use `HandleContext` like below.
391	
392	```go
393	r.GET("/test", func(c *gin.Context) {
394	    c.Request.URL.Path = "/test2"
395	    r.HandleContext(c)
396	})
397	r.GET("/test2", func(c *gin.Context) {
398	    c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"hello": "world"})
399	})
400	```

402	## Middleware
403	
404	> Configure middleware for request processing, authentication, and error recovery.
405	
406	### Blank Gin without middleware by default
407	
408	Use
409	
410	```go
411	r := gin.New()
412	```
413	
414	instead of
415	
416	```go
417	// Default With the Logger and Recovery middleware already attached
418	r := gin.Default()
419	```
420	
421	### Using middleware
422	
423	```go
424	func main() {
425	  // Creates a router without any middleware by default
426	  r := gin.New()
427	
428	  // Global middleware
429	  // Logger middleware will write the logs to gin.DefaultWriter even if you set with GIN_MODE=release.
430	  // By default gin.DefaultWriter = os.Stdout
431	  r.Use(gin.Logger())
432	
433	  // Recovery middleware recovers from any panics and writes a 500 if there was one.
434	  r.Use(gin.Recovery())
435	
436	  // Per route middleware, you can add as many as you desire.
437	  r.GET("/benchmark", MyBenchLogger(), benchEndpoint)
438	
439	  // Authorization group
440	  // authorized := r.Group("/", AuthRequired())
441	  // exactly the same as:
442	  authorized := r.Group("/")
443	  // per group middleware! in this case we use the custom created
444	  // AuthRequired() middleware just in the "authorized" group.
445	  authorized.Use(AuthRequired())
446	  {
447	    authorized.POST("/login", loginEndpoint)
448	    authorized.POST("/submit", submitEndpoint)
449	    authorized.POST("/read", readEndpoint)
450	
451	    // nested group
452	    testing := authorized.Group("testing")
453	    // visit 0.0.0.0:8080/testing/analytics
454	    testing.GET("/analytics", analyticsEndpoint)
455	  }
456	
457	  // Listen and serve on 0.0.0.0:8080
458	  r.Run(":8080")
459	}
460	```
461	
462	### Custom Middleware
463	
464	```go
465	func Logger() gin.HandlerFunc {
466	  return func(c *gin.Context) {
467	    t := time.Now()
468	
469	    // Set example variable
470	    c.Set("example", "12345")
471	
472	    // before request
473	
474	    c.Next()
475	
476	    // after request
477	    latency := time.Since(t)
478	    log.Print(latency)
479	
480	    // access the status we are sending
481	    status := c.Writer.Status()
482	    log.Println(status)
483	  }
484	}
485	
486	func main() {
487	  r := gin.New()
488	  r.Use(Logger())
489	
490	  r.GET("/test", func(c *gin.Context) {
491	    example := c.MustGet("example").(string)
492	
493	    // it would print: "12345"
494	    log.Println(example)
495	  })
496	
497	  // Listen and serve on 0.0.0.0:8080
498	  r.Run(":8080")
499	}
500	```

508

812	## Request Binding & Validation
813	
814	> Bind and validate request data from query strings, forms, JSON, and more.
815	
816	### Model binding and validation
817	
818	To bind a request body into a type, use model binding. We currently support binding of JSON, XML, YAML, TOML and standard form values (foo=bar&boo=baz).
819	
820	Gin uses [**go-playground/validator/v10**](https://github.com/go-playground/validator) for validation. Check the full docs on tags usage [here](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-playground/validator#hdr-Baked_In_Validators_and_Tags).
821	
822	Note that you need to set the corresponding binding tag on all fields you want to bind. For example, when binding from JSON, set `json:"fieldname"`.
823	
824	Also, Gin provides two sets of methods for binding:
825	
826	- **Type** - Must bind
827	  - **Methods** - `Bind`, `BindJSON`, `BindXML`, `BindQuery`, `BindYAML`, `BindHeader`, `BindTOML`
828	  - **Behavior** - These methods use `MustBindWith` under the hood. If there is a binding error, the request is aborted with `c.AbortWithError(400, err).SetType(ErrorTypeBind)`. This sets the response status code to 400 and the `Content-Type` header is set to `text/plain; charset=utf-8`. Note that if you try to set the response code after this, it will result in a warning `[GIN-debug] [WARNING] Headers were already written. Wanted to override status code 400 with 422`. If you wish to have greater control over the behavior, consider using the `ShouldBind` equivalent method.
829	- **Type** - Should bind
830	  - **Methods** - `ShouldBind`, `ShouldBindJSON`, `ShouldBindXML`, `ShouldBindQuery`, `ShouldBindYAML`, `ShouldBindHeader`, `ShouldBindTOML`,
831	  - **Behavior** - These methods use `ShouldBindWith` under the hood. If there is a binding error, the error is returned and it is the developer's responsibility to handle the request and error appropriately.
832	
833	When using the Bind-method, Gin tries to infer the binder depending on the Content-Type header. If you are sure what you are binding, you can use `MustBindWith` or `ShouldBindWith`.
834	
835	You can also specify that specific fields are required. If a field is decorated with `binding:"required"` and has an empty value when binding, an error will be returned.
836	
837	```go
838	// Binding from JSON
839	type Login struct {
840	  User     string `form:"user" json:"user" xml:"user" binding:"required"`
841	  Password string `form:"password" json:"password" xml:"password" binding:"required"`
842	}
843	
844	func main() {
845	  router := gin.Default()
846	
847	  // Example for binding JSON ({"user": "manu", "password": "123"})
848	  router.POST("/loginJSON", func(c *gin.Context) {
849	    var json Login
850	    if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&json); err != nil {
851	      c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": err.Error()})
852	      return
853	    }
854	
855	    if json.User != "manu" || json.Password != "123" {
856	      c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, gin.H{"status": "unauthorized"})
857	      return
858	    }
859	
860	    c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"status": "you are logged in"})
861	  })
862	
863	  // Example for binding XML (
864	  //  <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
865	  //  <root>
866	  //    <user>manu</user>
867	  //    <password>123</password>
868	  //  </root>)
869	  router.POST("/loginXML", func(c *gin.Context) {
870	    var xml Login
871	    if err := c.ShouldBindXML(&xml); err != nil {
872	      c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": err.Error()})
873	      return
874	    }
875	
876	    if xml.User != "manu" || xml.Password != "123" {
877	      c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, gin.H{"status": "unauthorized"})
878	      return
879	    }
880	
881	    c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"status": "you are logged in"})
882	  })
883	
884	  // Example for binding a HTML form (user=manu&password=123)
885	  router.POST("/loginForm", func(c *gin.Context) {
886	    var form Login
887	    // This will infer what binder to use depending on the content-type header.
888	    if err := c.ShouldBind(&form); err != nil {
889	      c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": err.Error()})
890	      return
891	    }
892	
893	    if form.User != "manu" || form.Password != "123" {
894	      c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, gin.H{"status": "unauthorized"})
895	      return
896	    }
897	
898	    c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"status": "you are logged in"})
899	  })
900	
901	  // Listen and serve on 0.0.0.0:8080
902	  router.Run(":8080")
903	}
904	```

931	### Custom Validators
932	
933	It is also possible to register custom validators. See the [example code](https://github.com/gin-gonic/examples/tree/master/custom-validation/server.go).
934	
935	```go
936	package main
937	
938	import (
939	  "net/http"
940	  "time"
941	
942	  "github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
943	  "github.com/gin-gonic/gin/binding"
944	  "github.com/go-playground/validator/v10"
945	)
946	
947	// Booking contains binded and validated data.
948	type Booking struct {
949	  CheckIn  time.Time `form:"check_in" binding:"required,bookabledate" time_format:"2006-01-02"`
950	  CheckOut time.Time `form:"check_out" binding:"required,gtfield=CheckIn" time_format:"2006-01-02"`
951	}
952	
953	var bookableDate validator.Func = func(fl validator.FieldLevel) bool {
954	  date, ok := fl.Field().Interface().(time.Time)
955	  if ok {
956	    today := time.Now()
957	    if today.After(date) {
958	      return false
959	    }
960	  }
961	  return true
962	}
963	
964	func main() {
965	  route := gin.Default()
966	
967	  if v, ok := binding.Validator.Engine().(*validator.Validate); ok {
968	    v.RegisterValidation("bookabledate", bookableDate)
969	  }
970	
971	  route.GET("/bookable", getBookable)
972	  route.Run(":8085")
973	}
974	
975	func getBookable(c *gin.Context) {
976	  var b Booking
977	  if err := c.ShouldBindWith(&b, binding.Query); err == nil {
978	    c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"message": "Booking dates are valid!"})
979	  } else {
980	    c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": err.Error()})
981	  }
982	}
983	```

1231	### Bind custom unmarshaler
1232	
1233	To override gin's default binding logic, define a function on your type that satisfies the `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` interface from the Golang standard library. Then specify `parser=encoding.TextUnmarshaler` in the `uri`/`form` tag of the field being bound.
1234	
1235	```go
1236	package main
1237	
1238	import (
1239	  "encoding"
1240	  "strings"
1241	
1242	  "github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
1243	)
1244	
1245	type Birthday string
1246	
1247	func (b *Birthday) UnmarshalText(text []byte) error {
1248	  *b = Birthday(strings.Replace(string(text), "-", "/", -1))
1249	  return nil
1250	}
1251	
1252	var _ encoding.TextUnmarshaler = (*Birthday)(nil) //assert Birthday implements encoding.TextUnmarshaler
1253	
1254	func main() {
1255	  route := gin.Default()
1256	  var request struct {
1257	    Birthday         Birthday   `form:"birthday,parser=encoding.TextUnmarshaler"`
1258	    Birthdays        []Birthday `form:"birthdays,parser=encoding.TextUnmarshaler" collection_format:"csv"`
1259	    BirthdaysDefault []Birthday `form:"birthdaysDef,default=2020-09-01;2020-09-02,parser=encoding.TextUnmarshaler" collection_format:"csv"`
1260	  }
1261	  route.GET("/test", func(ctx *gin.Context) {
1262	    _ = ctx.BindQuery(&request)
1263	    ctx.JSON(200, request)
1264	  })
1265	  _ = route.Run(":8088")
1266	}
1267	```
1268	
1269	Test it with:
1270	
1271	```sh
1272	curl 'localhost:8088/test?birthday=2000-01-01&birthdays=2000-01-01,2000-01-02'
1273	```
1274	
1275	Result
1276	
1277	```sh
1278	{"Birthday":"2000/01/01","Birthdays":["2000/01/01","2000/01/02"],"BirthdaysDefault":["2020/09/01","2020/09/02"]}
1279	```

1281	Note:
1282	
1283	- If `parser=encoding.TextUnmarshaler` is specified for a type that does **not** implement `encoding.TextUnmarshaler`, gin will ignore it and proceed with its default binding logic.
1284	- If `parser=encoding.TextUnmarshaler` is specified for a type and that type's implementation of `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` returns an error, gin will stop binding and return the error to the client.

1313	    Birthdays        []Birthday `form:"birthdays" collection_format:"csv"`
1314	    BirthdaysDefault []Birthday `form:"birthdaysDef,default=2020-09-01;2020-09-02" collection_format:"csv"`

1544	### Try to bind body into different structs
1545	
1546	The normal methods for binding request body consumes `c.Request.Body` and they
1547	cannot be called multiple times.
1548	
1549	```go
1550	type formA struct {
1551	  Foo string `json:"foo" xml:"foo" binding:"required"`
1552	}
1553	
1554	type formB struct {
1555	  Bar string `json:"bar" xml:"bar" binding:"required"`
1556	}
1557	
1558	func SomeHandler(c *gin.Context) {
1559	  objA := formA{}
1560	  objB := formB{}
1561	  // Calling c.ShouldBind consumes c.Request.Body and it cannot be reused.
1562	  if errA := c.ShouldBind(&objA); errA == nil {
1563	    c.String(http.StatusOK, `the body should be formA`)
1564	  // Always an error is occurred by this because c.Request.Body is EOF now.
1565	  } else if errB := c.ShouldBind(&objB); errB == nil {
1566	    c.String(http.StatusOK, `the body should be formB`)
1567	  } else {
1568	    ...
1569	  }
1570	}
1571	```
1572	
1573	For this, you can use `c.ShouldBindBodyWith` or shortcuts.
1574	
1575	- `c.ShouldBindBodyWithJSON` is a shortcut for c.ShouldBindBodyWith(obj, binding.JSON).
1576	- `c.ShouldBindBodyWithXML` is a shortcut for c.ShouldBindBodyWith(obj, binding.XML).
1577	- `c.ShouldBindBodyWithYAML` is a shortcut for c.ShouldBindBodyWith(obj, binding.YAML).
1578	- `c.ShouldBindBodyWithTOML` is a shortcut for c.ShouldBindBodyWith(obj, binding.TOML).
1579	
1580	```go
1581	func SomeHandler(c *gin.Context) {
1582	  objA := formA{}
1583	  objB := formB{}
1584	  // This reads c.Request.Body and stores the result into the context.
1585	  if errA := c.ShouldBindBodyWith(&objA, binding.Form); errA == nil {
1586	    c.String(http.StatusOK, `the body should be formA`)
1587	  // At this time, it reuses body stored in the context.
1588	  } else if errB := c.ShouldBindBodyWith(&objB, binding.JSON); errB == nil {
1589	    c.String(http.StatusOK, `the body should be formB JSON`)
1590	  // And it can accepts other formats
1591	  } else if errB2 := c.ShouldBindBodyWithXML(&objB); errB2 == nil {
1592	    c.String(http.StatusOK, `the body should be formB XML`)
1593	  } else {
1594	    ...
1595	  }
1596	}
1597	```
1598	
1599	1. `c.ShouldBindBodyWith` stores body into the context before binding. This has
1600	   a slight impact to performance, so you should not use this method if you are
1601	   enough to call binding at once.
1602	2. This feature is only needed for some formats -- `JSON`, `XML`, `MsgPack`,
1603	   `ProtoBuf`. For other formats, `Query`, `Form`, `FormPost`, `FormMultipart`,
1604	   can be called by `c.ShouldBind()` multiple times without any damage to
1605	   performance (See [#1341](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/pull/1341)).
